quickAnswer: To calculate the percentage change between an old number and a new number, subtract the old value from the new value, divide that difference by the absolute value of the old number, and multiply by 100. The tool also supports percent difference, parts of a whole, and direct percentage values.

formula.title: Percentage Change & Difference Formulas
formula.expression: Percentage Change = ((New Value - Old Value) / |Old Value|) × 100
formula.explanation: Subtract the original baseline value (Old) from the ending value (New) to obtain the raw difference. Divide by the absolute value of the old number to preserve direction, then multiply by 100. For comparisons without a baseline, percentage difference divides absolute difference by the mean of both numbers.

commonMistakes.title: Dividing by the New Value
commonMistakes.description: Always divide by the original starting baseline (Old Value). Dividing by the new value gives the fraction of the final number, producing an incorrect percentage.

commonMistakes.title: Confusing Percentage Points with Percentage Change
commonMistakes.description: If tax rises from 10% to 12%, that is a 2 percentage point increase, but a 20% relative percentage increase ((12 - 10) / 10 = 0.20).

commonMistakes.title: Assuming Inverse Symmetry
commonMistakes.description: A 50% drop requires a 100% gain to break even. If a $100 stock falls 50% to $50, gaining 50% only returns it to $75.

commonMistakes.title: Attempting to Calculate Change from Zero
commonMistakes.description: Division by zero is mathematically undefined. You cannot calculate relative percentage change from an initial baseline of zero.

faqs.q: How do you find the percent change between two numbers?
faqs.a: Subtract the old number from the new number, divide the result by the old number, and multiply by 100. For example, going from 7 to 13 is (13 − 7) ÷ 7 × 100 = 85.7%.

faqs.q: Is it a percent increase or decrease?
faqs.a: Look at the sign of the result. If the new number is bigger than the old number, the percent change is positive and it is an increase. If the new number is smaller, the result is negative and it is a decrease. Going from 60 to 40 gives −33.3%, a 33% decrease.

faqs.q: What is the difference between percentage change and percentage points?
faqs.a: Decide whether you need percentage points or percent change. Percentage points are the simple difference between two percentages: a rate moving from 10% to 12% rose by 2 percentage points. Percent change compares that difference to the starting rate: (12 − 10) ÷ 10 × 100 = a 20% increase.

faqs.q: Why can't percentage change be calculated when starting from zero?
faqs.a: The percentage change formula divides the difference by the initial value: ((New - Old) / |Old|) × 100. When the old value is zero, division by zero occurs, which is mathematically undefined.

faqs.q: What is the difference between percentage change and percentage difference?
faqs.a: Percentage change has a chronological direction (old value to new value). Percentage difference compares two values where neither is considered the baseline or original, dividing the absolute difference by the average of the two numbers.
Yes. Any time a quantity more than doubles, the percentage change exceeds +100%. For instance, increasing from 20 to 60 is a +200% increase.

For standard positive physical quantities (like prices or weight), a decrease cannot exceed 100% because dropping by 100% brings the value to zero. Decreases beyond -100% only occur when quantities move into negative numbers.

faqs.q: How does the tool handle negative baseline numbers?
faqs.a: The formula uses the absolute value of the baseline in the denominator: ((New - Old) / |Old|) × 100. This ensures that moving from -100 to -50 correctly registers as an increase (+50%).

faqs.q: Can I use this calculator for year-over-year (YoY) revenue calculations?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter last year's revenue in the Old Value field and this year's revenue in the New Value field to compute YoY business growth.

how-to-calculate-percentage-change-betwe.li1: Find the difference: subtract the old number from the new number (new − old).
how-to-calculate-percentage-change-betwe.li2: Divide by the old number: divide that difference by the starting value.
how-to-calculate-percentage-change-betwe.li3: Multiply by 100: the result is the percent change. A positive answer is an increase; a negative answer is a decrease.
how-to-calculate-percentage-change-betwe.p1: For example, from 7 to 13: (13 − 7) ÷ 7 × 100 = 85.7%, about an 86% increase.

formula.mode1:
Formula: Percentage Change = ((New - Old) / |Old|) × 100

Step-by-step:
1. Difference = {{new}} - {{old}} = {{diff}}
2. Divide by |Initial| = {{diff}} / |{{old}}| = {{ratio}}
3. Multiply by 100 = {{pct}}%
formula.mode2:
Formula: Final Value = Starting Value {{sign}} (Starting Value × (Percentage / 100))

Step-by-step:
1. Delta = {{base}} × ({{pct}} / 100) = {{delta}}
2. Final = {{base}} {{sign}} {{delta}} = {{final}}
formula.mode3:
Formula: Percentage = (X / Y) × 100

Step-by-step:
1. Divide X by Y = {{x}} / {{y}} = {{ratio}}
2. Multiply by 100 = {{ratio}} × 100 = {{pct}}%
formula.mode4:
Formula: Percent Difference = (|V1 - V2| / ((V1 + V2) / 2)) × 100

Step-by-step:
1. |V1 - V2| = |{{a}} - {{b}}| = {{diff}}
2. Average = ({{a}} + {{b}}) / 2 = {{average}}
3. Divide and multiply by 100 = ({{diff}} / {{average}}) × 100 = {{pct}}%
